bull.b: Consistent, growing free cash flow (~$170M TTM and a record quarter) provides durable internal funding for R&D, security and cloud expansion. Strong FCF lowers refinancing risk, funds strategic investments, and supports operational resilience even while GAAP profits are still improving.

Sustained high gross margins reflect scalable software economics and efficient artifact delivery. Combined with subscription and cloud revenue, this margin profile supports profitable unit economics, funds customer success and product development, and makes cash conversion durable as scale increases.

bull.t: Rapid cloud expansion and enterprise upsell
bull.b: A strong shift to cloud and growing large-account cohort (higher RPO and net-dollar-retention) improves recurring revenue predictability and upsell runway. Enterprise adoption and security attach rates create multi-year revenue visibility and increase lifetime value per customer, supporting durable growth.

bear.b: Despite improving margins and non-GAAP profitability, persistent GAAP losses mean return metrics remain negative. This constrains long-term capital allocation flexibility, increases sensitivity to cost pressures, and leaves the company reliant on continued margin expansion to demonstrate durable earnings quality.

A large self-hosted customer base raises operational and security burdens, as illustrated by a recent zero-day. This complicates efforts to migrate customers to higher-margin cloud offerings, increases remediation costs and customer scrutiny, and can slow enterprise conversions and product standardization.

Rising AI-driven consumption and on-demand usage create volatile, hard-to-predict revenue patterns and reliance on converting overages to committed contracts. That variability, plus derisking of large deals, can delay revenue recognition and reduce near-term visibility despite strong pipeline metrics.
